catalog_quote: Word-stress normally falls on the penultimate or antepenultimate syllable. Stress on final syllables is generally avoided in Sardinian. Indeed, a final epenthetic vowel is added to Latin monosyllables to yield paroxytonic forms. ... However, oxytonic forms do arise, mainly in Campidanese and Logudorese, as a result of elision of an intervocalic consonant: Log. /'pe/ (< pedem) 'foot', Camp. /dro'mi/ (< dOrmIre) 'to sleep'. A further process which yields final stress is truncation of the post-tonic sequence in vocative uses of nouns (particularly proper names and diminutives) and certain imperatives: /ju'a/ (<- /ju'anne/ 'John'), /pitsin'ne/ (<- /pitsin'neddu, -a/ 'little boy/ girl'), /a'ba/ (<- /a'barra/ 'stay'), /'te/ (<- /'tene/ 'hold'). When a verb (e.g. an imperative) is followed by a single clitic, the verb retains its normal stress pattern. However, if two or more clitics are added…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is lexically fixed within the last three syllables, as in Italian: the vast majority of words are paroxytone (penultimate stress); antepenultimate and final stress exist and must be marked orthographically because they are not predictable from the word shape.
new_statements.exceptions: Words with final and antepenultimate stress exist as the marked minority (they get a graphic accent); example figiu ['fidʒu] 'son' is paroxytone.
new_statements.identity_note: Lai 2002 describes the Nuoro (Nuorese) dialect specifically (its lexical counts come from a Nuorese dictionary sample; fn. 162 says Contini's 1970a counts for Nughedu, Logudorese, are close). Vanrell et al. 2014 record Logudorese and Campidanese speakers but state the paroxytone generalization for Sardinian as a whole. Molinu 2021 speaks of 'le sarde' generally (her own fieldwork is Logudorese, Buddusò). Hofmann 1885 cites both Logudorese and Campidanese forms. None of the sources restricts the placement statement to a single village.

new_statements.relation_note: Nuoro (Nuorese) variety specifically. Compatible with Vanrell et al. 2014 and fills the empty catalog rule with quantified placement: penultimate default, lexical antepenultimate, final stress marginal and repaired.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is lexical (Romance type), overwhelmingly penultimate: table A on p. 52, counted over a 4000-entry Nuorese dictionary sample, gives paroxytones 21% (2-syll.) + 31% (3-syll.) + 28% (4-syll.) + 7% (5-syll.) + 1% (6-syll.) + 0.03% (7-syll.), i.e. about 88%; proparoxytones 7.5% + 4% + 0.6% + 0.2%, about 12%; oxytones 0.1% (monosyllables) + 0.03% (trisyllables); pre-proparoxytones 0.03%. Final stress is essentially banned: the few oxytones (ki, tu, da, kaffe..) receive a paragogic vowel ([kie], [tue], [dae]) so that the word surfaces as paroxytone.

new_statements.exceptions: Rare oxytones (loans such as caffe, place names such as Buddusò) repaired by a paragogic vowel; fn. 163 p. 52 notes that certain trisyllabic verbs keep their stress when clitics are added ([narramilu] 'tell it to me', after Wagner 1984 [1941] §§ 11-12); fn. 162 says Contini's (1970a) counts for Nughedu are close to these.

new_statements.quote: De même, s'il existe en sarde une contrainte sur l'oxytonèse qui est respectée par ailleurs38, pourquoi ces formes ne sont pas réparées via l'épenthèse vocalique ? [fn. 38:] Comme le montre la réparation, via épenthèse, des formes oytones et subminimales ki >kie, mi > mie, tu > tue, etc. (Molinu 1999a[A]). (p. 55) [...] En effet, le mot minimal, en sarde, est constitué d'un trochée dissyllabique et cette contrainte est transgressée par les impératifs, les vocatifs et les interjections. (p. 56) [...] le pattern accentuel (oxytonie), des fausses paires minimales ([an'tɔ] (< [an'tɔna]) « Anto(nia)! » vs [an'to] (< [an'toni]) « Anto(ine)! ») (p. 56)
new_statements.translation: Likewise, if in Sardinian there is a constraint against oxytony that is otherwise respected [fn. 38: as shown by the repair, through epenthesis, of oxytone and subminimal forms ki > kie, mi > mie, tu > tue, etc. (Molinu 1999a)], why are these forms not repaired by vowel epenthesis? [...] Indeed the minimal word in Sardinian consists of a disyllabic trochee, and this constraint is violated by imperatives, vocatives and interjections. [...] the accentual pattern (oxytony), the false minimal pairs ([an'tɔ] (< [an'tɔna]) 'Anto(nia)!' vs [an'to] (< [an'toni]) 'Anto(ine)!')

new_statements.rule_in_words: Sardinian has a constraint against final (oxytone) stress that is normally enforced by vowel epenthesis (ki > kie, tu > tue), and a minimal-word requirement of a disyllabic trochee, i.e. the unmarked word ends in a stressed-unstressed sequence (penultimate stress). Where stress falls among the last syllables is otherwise lexical.
new_statements.exceptions: Truncated imperatives (na' < nara 'say!', le' < lea 'take!', mi < mira 'look!'), vocatives (oxytonic truncations [an'tɔ], [an'to]) and interjections violate both the anti-oxytone constraint and the minimal-word trochee; they sit at the periphery of the system.

new_statements.translation: A. Stress. In the following points the stress deviates from Latin: 1) The infinitives of the Latin 2nd conjugation, as in Catalan and by analogy with the infinitives of the Latin 3rd conjugation, throw the accent from the ending onto the stem syllable, without exception. [...] 2) Sardinian follows the general Romance tendency of placing the accent, in the 1st and 2nd plural present of the Latin 3rd conjugation, on the penultimate inflectional syllable. [...] 3) Some proparoxytones of the Latin 1st conjugation have in the singular present the Spanish accent, i.e. they become paroxytones: toleras, continuat, consideras, Logudorese and Campidanese. (Items 4-5 add stress retraction by one syllable in the 1st/2nd pl. imperfect subjunctive, Campidanese and Logudorese.)

tone_statements.citation: Lai, Jean-Pierre (2003). Le sarde de Nuoro au sein du nouvel Atlas multimédia prosodique de l'espace roman (AMPER). Géolinguistique 9, 145-187.
tone_statements.quote: Nous avons très souvent relevé des pics de FO, dont le poids dans la détection de l’accent devrait être prépondérant, qui ne coïncident pas avec les voyelles toniques mais avec les post-toniques et, plus fréquemment, les pré¬ toniques.
tone_statements.translation: We very often found F0 peaks -- whose weight in the detection of the accent ought to be preponderant -- that do not coincide with the tonic vowels but with the post-tonic and, more frequently, the pretonic ones. (Persee uncorrected scanned; 'pré¬ toniques' = 'prétoniques' hyphenated across a line.)
tone_statements.locator: p. 153, section 'Pour la fréquence fondamentale (F0)', first paragraph; conclusions p. 178
tone_statements.summary: Lexical stress (mostly paroxytone, some proparoxytone, oxytones avoided); F0 marks sentence modality and phrasing, peaks often on pre-/post-tonic syllables; no lexical tone.

tone_statements.citation: Contini, Michel (1992). Vers une géoprosodie. In Gotzon Aurrekoetxea & Xarles Videgain (eds.), Nazioarteko Dialektologia Biltzarra. Agiriak (Bilbo, 1991.X.21/25) (Iker 7), 83-109. Bilbo: Euskaltzaindia / Real Academia de la Lengua Vasca.
tone_statements.quote: l'accentuation et l'intonation. Sur le plan de la substance, l'une et l'autre se réalisent par les mêmes paramètres physiques, à savoir la fréquence laryngienne (Fo), l'intensité (I) et la durée (D) … L'analyse de très nombreux tracés de langues à accent mobile (italien, sarde, espagnol, gree moderne en particulier) semble indiquer que la variabilité d'un même mot prosodique place aux frontières majeures, dans des phrases de moda[ités différentes, affecte surtout les syllabes qui vont de la syllabe accentuée, voire même de la syllabe préaecentuelle, à la dernière (comprises).
tone_statements.translation: [accentuation and intonation.] In substance, both are realised by the same physical parameters, namely laryngeal frequency (F0), intensity (I) and duration (D) … The analysis of very many traces of mobile-accent languages (Italian, Sardinian, Spanish, Modern Greek in particular) seems to show that the variability of one and the same prosodic word placed at major boundaries, in sentences of different modalities, mainly affects the syllables running from the accented syllable, or even the pre-accentual syllable, to the last one (inclusive).
tone_statements.locator: p. 85 and p. 88; Sardinian statement/question passage p. 86 referring to Planche 2, p. 99
tone_statements.summary: Stress language (mobile lexical stress); F0 contours are intonational (modality marked from the first prosodic word); no lexical tone.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation and all auxiliary snippets (pp. 316, 326-327, 333) are present verbatim at the stated places in the held archive.org scanned text of Jones 1988; the compilers independent confirmation stands. (2) Deciding source: a 1988 handbook grammar sketch by a Sardinian specialist, explicitly describing Logudorese-Nuorese (Lula), so languoid identity is correct; it is reputable but not the fullest or most recent phonological description (Molinu 2017, Contini 1987, Pittau 1972, Corda 1994, Mensching & Remberger 2016 exist; none held, none open). (3) Open sources downloaded now — Lai 2002 (instrumental thesis on Nuoro prosody, HAL), Molinu 2021 (HDR synthesis, HAL), Vanrell et al. 2014 (Loquens, OA), Hofmann 1885 (archive.org) — all either confirm or are silent: stress type is a lexical property within the last three syllables, paroxytones dominate (Lai's lexicon counts)

sources.citation: Molinu, Lucia (2021). Contraintes et variation en sarde et ailleurs. Mémoire de synthèse pour l'Habilitation à diriger des recherches, Université Toulouse Jean Jaurès. 137 pp. HAL tel-03348417.
sources.quote: Synthesis of Molinu's work on (mainly Logudorese, Buddusò) Sardinian phonology. States a constraint against oxytony in Sardinian, repaired by vowel epenthesis (ki > kie, mi > mie, tu > tue; fn. 38), a disyllabic-trochee minimal word, and that truncated monosyllabic imperatives (mi' < mira, na' < nara, te' < tene) and truncated vocatives ([an'tɔ] < [an'tɔna]) are oxytone forms at the periphery of the system that escape repair. No general stress-placement algorithm is given; stress position is treated as lexical (proparoxytone vs paroxytone verb types discussed pp. 80-82).

sources.quote: Historical Lautlehre (Glottolog hhtype phonology). The only stress section lists where verb stress deviates from Latin: 2nd-conj. infinitives retract stress to the stem (ténnere, párrere), 1/2pl present of Latin 3rd conj. stress the penultimate (leghímus), some Latin proparoxytone presents become paroxytone (consíderas), Logudorese 1/2pl imperfect subjunctive shifts stress one syllable forward (timerémus). No synchronic word-stress rule; consistent with lexically/morphologically specified stress.

sources.quote: l'accentuation et l'intonation. Sur le plan de la substance, l'une et l'autre se réalisent par les mêmes paramètres physiques, à savoir la fréquence laryngienne (Fo), l'intensité (I) et la durée (D) … L'analyse de très nombreux tracés de langues à accent mobile (italien, sarde, espagnol, gree moderne en particulier) semble indiquer que la variabilité d'un même mot prosodique place aux frontières majeures, dans des phrases de moda[ités différentes, affecte surtout les syllabes qui vont de la syllabe accentuée, voire même de la syllabe préaecentuelle, à la dernière (comprises).
sources.locator: p. 85 and p. 88; Sardinian statement/question passage p. 86 referring to Planche 2, p. 99
sources.note: No lexical tone described: Sardinian is classed with Italian, Spanish and Modern Greek as a mobile (lexical) stress language; F0, intensity and duration realise word accent and sentence intonation. (statement read as group-level, not specific to this language).

tone.quote: l'accentuation et l'intonation. Sur le plan de la substance, l'une et l'autre se réalisent par les mêmes paramètres physiques, à savoir la fréquence laryngienne (Fo), l'intensité (I) et la durée (D) … L'analyse de très nombreux tracés de langues à accent mobile (italien, sarde, espagnol, gree moderne en particulier) semble indiquer que la variabilité d'un même mot prosodique place aux frontières majeures, dans des phrases de moda[ités différentes, affecte surtout les syllabes qui vont de la syllabe accentuée, voire même de la syllabe préaecentuelle, à la dernière (comprises).
tone.locator: p. 85 and p. 88; Sardinian statement/question passage p. 86 referring to Planche 2, p. 99
tone.translation: [accentuation and intonation.] In substance, both are realised by the same physical parameters, namely laryngeal frequency (F0), intensity (I) and duration (D) … The analysis of very many traces of mobile-accent languages (Italian, Sardinian, Spanish, Modern Greek in particular) seems to show that the variability of one and the same prosodic word placed at major boundaries, in sentences of different modalities, mainly affects the syllables running from the accented syllable, or even the pre-accentual syllable, to the last one (inclusive).
tone.summary: Stress language (mobile lexical stress); F0 contours are intonational (modality marked from the first prosodic word); no lexical tone.
tone.says: No lexical tone described: Sardinian is classed with Italian, Spanish and Modern Greek as a mobile (lexical) stress language; F0, intensity and duration realise word accent and sentence intonation. (statement read as group-level, not specific to this language).
